rationale:
Split into seven children. The supplied proof has three independent analytic layers, plus a short Lean assembly.
Layer 1 — geometry of the rectifiable carrier (parent Steps 2–3, Simon 4.1–4.4):
- `slicing_im_tangential_gradient` constructs a Borel tangential gradient G of the McShane extension of f.
- `slicing_im_coarea` is the co-area formula on M with Jacobian |G|.
- `slicing_im_slice_triple` (depends on coarea) shows that for a.e. t, (M_t, θ, ξ⌞(G/|G|)), with M_t = {x∈M : f x = t, G x ≠ 0}, is a rectifiable m-triple in U.
Layer 2 — Lemma 4.5(2) for an arbitrary S (parent Step 4(1)–(5)):
- `slicing_im_lipschitz_leibniz` is Simon's mollification/weak-convergence identity (1)–(3), stated for arbitrary representations of T and ∂T.
- `slicing_im_slice_identity` (depends on coarea and lipschitz_leibniz) covers the cut-off ψ_ε∘f, Remark 4.2 and Lebesgue points. For each test form ω, a.e. t, and every S with IsSlice T f t S, it gives S ω = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω, with a null set independent of S.
Layer 3 — removing the dependence on ω (parent Step 4(6)):
- `slicing_im_testform_determining`: a countable family of test forms determines currents.
- `slicing_im_tau_current`: a rectifiable triple defines a current.

Assembly: McShane extension (IsSlice only sees f on U), then children 1 and 6, then children 3 and 5. The countably many a.e. statements are combined with `ae_ball_iff`; child 7 gives the slice current, child 6 gives S equal to that current, and integrality follows from M_t ⊆ M. This assembly is kernel-checked in the exact comparator scope with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Children 2 and 4 are used through children 3 and 5. Dependencies are acyclic.
Deliberate deviation in Step 4(6): instead of C¹-density plus representation-coefficient estimates, child 6 uses density in the D(U) sequential topology, together with the built-in continuity of currents and child 7. This is closer to Simon's 'countable dense set of ω ∈ Dⁿ(U)' and needs no coefficient integrability.

Fact F (frame sign): if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the same k-dimensional subspace, τ'_i = Σ_j B_ij τ_j with B orthogonal, then by multilinearity and alternation simple(τ') = det(B)·simple(τ) and det B = ±1. TG(f, G) abbreviates the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and for every u ∈ Q the map s ↦ f(x + s u) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0.
1. Charts (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3). Since M is countably n-rectifiable, M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and N_j embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifolds of ℝ^P. Covering every N_j by countably many relatively compact coordinate patches we obtain countably many open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ and C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P which are Lipschitz on Ω_j and satisfy c_j|w − w'| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w')| (w, w' ∈ Ω_j, some c_j > 0), with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Consequently Φ_j|Ω_j is injective, DΦ_j(w) is injective for w ∈ Ω_j (|DΦ_j(w)u| ≥ c_j|u|), Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact hence Borel, (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz hence Borel, Φ_j maps Lⁿ-null subsets of Ω_j to Hⁿ-null sets and Φ_j⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ_j(Ω_j) to Lⁿ-null sets. Put A_j(w) := DΦ_j(w) and T_j(w) := range A_j(w) (an n-dimensional subspace). Define pairwise disjoint Borel sets V_j := Φ_j(Ω_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Φ_i(Ω_i); then Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j V_j) = 0.
2. (Rademacher in charts.) f∘Φ_j is Lipschitz on Ω_j (constant L·Lip(Φ_j|Ω_j)); extending it to a Lipschitz function on ℝⁿ (McShane, `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) and applying Rademacher's theorem (`LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`), using that Ω_j is open, f∘Φ_j is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω_j. Let D_j ⊆ Ω_j be the set of differentiability points; it is Borel (`measurableSet_of_differentiableAt`) and Lⁿ(Ω_j ∖ D_j) = 0, so Hⁿ(Φ_j(Ω_j ∖ D_j)) = 0.
3. (Definition of G.) For x ∈ V_j with w := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹(x) ∈ D_j put G(x) := A_j(w)(A_j(w)ᵀA_j(w))⁻¹∇(f∘Φ_j)(w), and put G(x) := 0 for all other x ∈ ℝ^P. Then G(x) ∈ T_j(w) and A_j(w)ᵀG(x) = ∇(f∘Φ_j)(w), i.e. ⟨G(x), A_j(w)u⟩ = D(f∘Φ_j)(w)u for all u ∈ ℝⁿ. G is Borel: Φ_j(D_j) is Borel as the image of a Borel set under the continuous injective map Φ_j|Ω_j (Lusin–Souslin, `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`), and on the Borel set V_j ∩ Φ_j(D_j) it is the composition of the Borel map (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ with the Borel map w ↦ A_j(w)(A_j(w)ᵀA_j(w))⁻¹∇(f∘Φ_j)(w) (DΦ_j is continuous, A_jᵀA_j is invertible on Ω_j, and w ↦ fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ_j) w is Borel by `measurable_fderiv`), and it is 0 on the complement of the countable union of these Borel sets.
4. Directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10). Let Φ be C¹ near w, x = Φ(w), F : ℝ^P → ℝ Lipschitz with constant C, and suppose F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, s ↦ F(x + s DΦ(w)u) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)u at s = 0: indeed F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(x) = [F(Φ(w+su)) − F(Φ(w))] + [F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(Φ(w+su))], the first bracket is sD(F∘Φ)(w)u + o(s), and the second is bounded by C|Φ(w) + sDΦ(w)u − Φ(w+su)| = o(s). Applied with F = f, Φ = Φ_j and w ∈ D_j it gives: for x = Φ_j(w) ∈ V_j and every v = A_j(w)u ∈ T_j(w), s ↦ f(x + sv) has derivative D(f∘Φ_j)(w)u = ⟨G(x), v⟩ at s = 0.
5. (Bound.) In the situation of Step 4, |f(x + sv) − f(x)| ≤ L|s||v|, so |⟨G(x), v⟩| ≤ L|v| for v ∈ T_j(w); taking v = G(x) ∈ T_j(w) gives |G(x)|² ≤ L|G(x)|, hence |G(x)| ≤ L. At all other points G = 0. So |G(x)| ≤ L for every x.
6. Tangent identification (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⟹' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version): if M' ⊆ U is Hᵏ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M' and θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M' ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, and Ψ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P is C¹ on an open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound on V, then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ Ψ(V) the pair (M', θ) has weighted approximate tangent plane range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x) at x. (For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), r^{-k}∫_{M'} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z) dHᵏ(z) splits into θ(x)·r^{-k}∫_{Ψ(V)} φ((z−x)/r) dHᵏ, which tends to θ(x)∫_{range DΨ} φ dHᵏ because Ψ(V) is a C¹ k-submanifold at x; the error r^{-k}∫_{M'∩Ψ(V)} φ(·)(θ − θ(x)) dHᵏ, which tends to 0 at Lebesgue points of θ for the Radon measure Hᵏ⌞(M'∩Ψ(V)∩K); and the parts over Ψ(V) ∖ M' and M' ∖ Ψ(V), which tend to 0 at Hᵏ-a.e. point of M' ∩ Ψ(V) by the upper-density theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, since Hᵏ⌞(Ψ(V)∖M') and θHᵏ⌞(M'∖Ψ(V)) are locally finite and vanish on M' ∩ Ψ(V).) Uniqueness at θ(x) > 0 then identifies every weighted approximate tangent plane at such x with range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x). Apply it with k = n, M' = M and Ψ = Φ_j, V = Ω_j: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j), every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q equals T_j((Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹x).
7. (Conclusion.) Let Z be the union of M ∖ ⋃_j V_j, the sets Φ_j(Ω_j ∖ D_j) and the exceptional sets of Step 6 (countably many Hⁿ-null sets), so Hⁿ(Z) = 0. Let x ∈ M ∖ Z. Then x ∈ V_j for some j, w := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹(x) ∈ D_j, and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x equals T_j(w). By Step 3, G(x) ∈ Q, and by Step 4, for every v ∈ Q, HasDerivAt (fun s ↦ f (x + s • v)) ⟨G(x), v⟩ 0. Together with Steps 3 and 5 (G Borel, |G| ≤ L everywhere) this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover M up to an Hⁿ-null set by countably many bi-Lipschitz C¹ charts Φ_j : Ω_j → ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3) and disjointify.
Rademacher: f∘Φ_j is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. on Ω_j; define G on each piece as the vector in range DΦ_j representing D(f∘Φ_j), 0 elsewhere (Borel).
Simon Ch. 2, 4.10: ambient directional derivatives of f along range DΦ_j equal D(f∘Φ_j)u = ⟨G, DΦ_j u⟩.
Lipschitz bound |G| ≤ L by testing with v = G(x).
Weighted tangent plane of (M, θ) equals range DΦ_j a.e. on each chart (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6, 1.8(1)) and is unique since θ > 0; conclude TG(f, G).

Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable there is a Borel B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (`NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`).
2. (C¹ approximation.) Fix j. f∘Φ_j is Lipschitz on Ω_j; let u_j be a Lipschitz extension to ℝⁿ (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`). By the C¹ approximation theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5) applied to u_j with ε = 1/k, k ≥ 1, there are C¹ functions h_{jk} : ℝⁿ → ℝ and Borel sets A_{jk} ⊆ Ω_j with Lⁿ(Ω_j ∖ ⋃_k A_{jk}) = 0 such that on A_{jk}: f∘Φ_j is differentiable, f∘Φ_j = h_{jk} and D(f∘Φ_j) = Dh_{jk}. (Take A_{jk} := Ω_j ∩ D ∩ {u_j = h_{jk}, ∇u_j = ∇h_{jk}} with D the Borel set of differentiability points of u_j.)
3. (Gradient identification.) Directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10). Let Φ be C¹ near w, x = Φ(w), F : ℝ^P → ℝ Lipschitz with constant C, and suppose F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, s ↦ F(x + s DΦ(w)u) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)u at s = 0: indeed F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(x) = [F(Φ(w+su)) − F(Φ(w))] + [F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(Φ(w+su))], the first bracket is sD(F∘Φ)(w)u + o(s), and the second is bounded by C|Φ(w) + sDΦ(w)u − Φ(w+su)| = o(s). Tangent identification (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⟹' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version): if M' ⊆ U is Hᵏ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M' and θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M' ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, and Ψ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P is C¹ on an open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound on V, then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ Ψ(V) the pair (M', θ) has weighted approximate tangent plane range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x) at x. (For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), r^{-k}∫_{M'} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z) dHᵏ(z) splits into θ(x)·r^{-k}∫_{Ψ(V)} φ((z−x)/r) dHᵏ, which tends to θ(x)∫_{range DΨ} φ dHᵏ because Ψ(V) is a C¹ k-submanifold at x; the error r^{-k}∫_{M'∩Ψ(V)} φ(·)(θ − θ(x)) dHᵏ, which tends to 0 at Lebesgue points of θ for the Radon measure Hᵏ⌞(M'∩Ψ(V)∩K); and the parts over Ψ(V) ∖ M' and M' ∖ Ψ(V), which tend to 0 at Hᵏ-a.e. point of M' ∩ Ψ(V) by the upper-density theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, since Hᵏ⌞(Ψ(V)∖M') and θHᵏ⌞(M'∖Ψ(V)) are locally finite and vanish on M' ∩ Ψ(V).) Uniqueness at θ(x) > 0 then identifies every weighted approximate tangent plane at such x with range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x). Applying the tangent identification with k = n, M' = M, Ψ = Φ_j, together with TG(f, G), we get an Hⁿ-null set Z_j such that for x ∈ (M ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk})) ∖ Z_j, w := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹(x): the weighted tangent plane is T_x = T_j(w), G(x) ∈ T_j(w), and for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨G(x), A_j(w)u⟩ = (d/ds) f(x + sA_j(w)u)|_{s=0} = D(f∘Φ_j)(w)u = Dh_{jk}(w)u. Let N_j := Φ_j(Ω_j), an embedded C¹ n-submanifold, and F_{jk} := h_{jk}∘(Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ : N_j → ℝ, a C¹ function on N_j. Its N_j-gradient at x = Φ_j(w) is the vector of T_j(w) representing u ↦ Dh_{jk}(w)u on A_j(w)u, so ∇^{N_j}F_{jk}(x) = G(x) and F_{jk}(x) = f(x) for those x.
4. (Pieces.) Enumerate the pairs (j, k) and let W_{jk} be the disjointification of the Borel sets (B ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk})) ∖ Z'_j, where Z'_j ⊇ Z_j is a Borel Hⁿ-null set (`toMeasurable`). The sets Φ_j(A_{jk}) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin, `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`), so the W_{jk} are pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of M, and Z := M ∖ ⋃ W_{jk} ⊆ (M ∖ B) ∪ (M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) ∪ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j ∖ ⋃_k A_{jk}) ∪ ⋃_j Z'_j is Hⁿ-null (Φ_j maps Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets).
5. (Null part, Eilenberg's inequality.) For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫* H^m(A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) dt ≤ c(m)·L·Hⁿ(A) (Federer 2.10.25). With A = Z this gives H^m(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t. For such t the sets M ∩ f⁻¹{t} and ⋃_{jk}(W_{jk} ∩ f⁻¹{t}) differ by an H^m-null set, so the restrictions of H^m to them coincide (`Measure.restrict_congr_set`), and, the W_{jk} ∩ f⁻¹{t} being disjoint Borel sets, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m = Σ_{jk} ∫_{W_{jk}∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m.
6. (C¹ co-area formula on a piece.) Fix (j, k). On the C¹ n-submanifold N_j the function F_{jk} is C¹ with co-area Jacobian J F_{jk} = |∇^{N_j}F_{jk}| (for a real-valued map, √det(dF∘dF*) = |∇F|). By the co-area formula for C¹ maps on C¹ submanifolds (Simon Ch. 2, 6.3 and its consequence 6.6 for non-negative measurable integrands; Federer 3.2.12, 3.2.22), for the Borel set W_{jk} ⊆ N_j and Borel g ≥ 0, the function t ↦ ∫_{W_{jk}∩F_{jk}⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is Lebesgue measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{W_{jk}∩F_{jk}⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_{W_{jk}} g |∇^{N_j}F_{jk}| dHⁿ. By Step 3 (F_{jk} = f and ∇^{N_j}F_{jk} = G on W_{jk}), W_{jk} ∩ F_{jk}⁻¹{t} = W_{jk} ∩ f⁻¹{t} and ∫_ℝ ∫_{W_{jk}∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_{W_{jk}} |G| g dHⁿ.
7. (Summation.) By Step 5 the function Ψ_g(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m agrees for L¹-a.e. t with the countable sum Σ_{jk} ∫_{W_{jk}∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m of Lebesgue-measurable [0,∞]-valued functions, hence is a.e.-measurable. By monotone convergence (`lintegral_tsum`) and Step 6, ∫_ℝ Ψ_g dt = Σ_{jk} ∫_{W_{jk}} |G| g dHⁿ = ∫_{⋃W_{jk}} |G| g dHⁿ = ∫_M |G| g dHⁿ, the last step because Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃ W_{jk}) = Hⁿ(Z) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Charts Φ_j and a Borel B ⊆ M of full measure (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3).
C¹ approximation of f∘Φ_j (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5): Borel A_{jk} where f∘Φ_j = h_{jk} with equal derivatives.
Simon Ch. 2, 4.10 and the weighted tangent identification: on the pieces, f = F_{jk} := h_{jk}∘Φ_j⁻¹ and ∇^{N_j}F_{jk} = G.
Eilenberg's inequality: the Hⁿ-null remainder has H^m-null slices for a.e. t.
C¹ co-area formula on each C¹ piece with Jacobian |∇^{N_j}F_{jk}| = |G| (Simon Ch. 2, 6.3, 6.6; Federer 3.2.22).
Sum over the disjoint Borel pieces (monotone convergence) and use a.e. equality for measurability.

subproblems.title: Slices of a rectifiable triple are rectifiable triples for a.e. t (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1–4.4)

For t ∈ ℝ let M_t := {x ∈ M : f(x) = t, G(x) ≠ 0} and let ξ_t(x) ∈ Λ_m be the interior product ξ(x)⌞ν(x), ν(x) := |G(x)|⁻¹G(x), i.e. ξ_t(x)(α) = ξ(x)(ν(x)♭∧α) for α ∈ Λ^m (in Lean: (ξ x).comp ((alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) m) (innerSL ℝ (‖G x‖⁻¹ • G x))))). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, IsRectifiableTriple U m M_t θ ξ_t holds.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P; Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure Lᵏ on ℝᵏ; H⁰ is counting measure by `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero` and `hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`). n := m+1. A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-form), ‖α‖ its operator norm; a k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k = (Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ); simple(τ) := simpleNVector τ, simple(τ)(α) = α(τ). For w ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^k put w♭∧α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α) ∈ Λ^{k+1}; by `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, (w♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i ⟨w, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_k); it is bilinear in (w, α), ‖w♭∧α‖ ≤ (k+1)|w|‖α‖, and it equals ((alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) k) (innerSL ℝ w))) α by `rfl`. Fact U: if τ is orthonormal and w = ±simple(τ) then |w(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖. Fact F (frame sign): if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the same k-dimensional subspace, τ'_i = Σ_j B_ij τ_j with B orthogonal, then by multilinearity and alternation simple(τ') = det(B)·simple(τ) and det B = ±1. IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ means: M ⊆ U; M is Hᵏ-null-measurable; M is countably k-rectifiable; θ > 0 on M; θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simple(τ). The weighted approximate tangent plane (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is unique at points where θ(x) ≠ 0 (SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`); when it exists at x ∈ M we call it T_x. TG(f, G) abbreviates the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and for every u ∈ Q the map s ↦ f(x + s u) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0.
We follow Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1 (whose printed proof uses Ch. 3, 2.10(2), Theorem 1.6 and the co-area formula), 4.3 and Definition 4.4. Throughout, 'a.e. t' means for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ; countably many such statements may be combined (`ae_all_iff`). The sibling `coarea` (co-area formula) applies to the present hypotheses verbatim.
1. (Null transfer, NT.) If Z ⊆ M and Hⁿ(Z) = 0 then H^m(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for a.e. t. Proof: let Z' := toMeasurable Hⁿ Z, a Borel set with Hⁿ(Z') = 0, and apply `coarea` to g := 1_{Z'}: ∫_ℝ H^m(Z' ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) dt = ∫_M |G|1_{Z'} dHⁿ ≤ L·Hⁿ(Z') = 0 (the inner integral of 1_{Z'} over M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is H^m(Z' ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) by `Measure.restrict_apply`). Hence H^m(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ H^m(Z' ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for a.e. t (Z ⊆ M).
2. (Exhaustion and Borel modifications.) Choose compacts K_i ⊆ U (i ≥ 1) such that every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i (U open). Since M ⊆ U = ⋃K_i and θ is integrable on each M ∩ K_i, θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (`aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff`); let θ̃, ξ̃ be Borel (strongly measurable) with θ = θ̃ and ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ-a.e. on M. Let B ⊆ M be Borel with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0. Z₁ := (M ∖ B) ∪ {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≠ θ̃(x) or ξ(x) ≠ ξ̃(x)} is Hⁿ-null.
3. (subset, pos.) For every t, M_t ⊆ M ⊆ U and θ > 0 on M_t.
4. (integrableOn.) Apply `coarea` to the Borel functions g_i := 1_{K_i}·ofReal(θ̃): ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g_i dH^m dt = ∫_M |G| g_i dHⁿ ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i} θ dHⁿ < ∞. Hence for a.e. t, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m < ∞ for all i. For such t which also satisfy NT for Z₁ (so H^m(Z₁ ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0), θ = θ̃ H^m-a.e. on M_t ∩ K_i ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i; as θ̃ is Borel, θ is H^m⌞(M_t ∩ K_i)-a.e. strongly measurable, and since θ > 0 on M_t, ∫_{M_t∩K_i} |θ| dH^m = ∫_{M_t∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m ≤ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m < ∞; so θ is H^m-integrable on M_t ∩ K_i. As every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i, θ is H^m-integrable on M_t ∩ K (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`).
5. (nullMeasurableSet.) M_t = (B ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ {G ≠ 0}) ∪ ((M ∖ B) ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ {G ≠ 0}); the first set is Borel (f continuous, G Borel) and the second is H^m-null for a.e. t by NT (Z₁ ⊇ M ∖ B). So M_t is H^m-null-measurable for a.e. t.
6. (aestronglyMeasurable.) The map x ↦ ι(x) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM).comp(smulRightL (innerSL ℝ (|G(x)|⁻¹G(x)))) ∈ L(Λ^m, Λ^{m+1}) is Borel (continuous linear operations applied to the Borel map x ↦ |G(x)|⁻¹G(x)), and composition of continuous linear maps is continuous; so ξ̃_t(x) := ξ̃(x).comp(ι(x)) is strongly measurable, and ξ_t = ξ̃_t on M_t ∖ Z₁. By NT, for a.e. t this is H^m-a.e. on M_t, so ξ_t is H^m⌞M_t-a.e. strongly measurable.
7. (Charts and C¹ approximations.) Charts (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3). Since M is countably n-rectifiable, M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and N_j embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifolds of ℝ^P. Covering every N_j by countably many relatively compact coordinate patches we obtain countably many open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ and C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P which are Lipschitz on Ω_j and satisfy c_j|w − w'| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w')| (w, w' ∈ Ω_j, some c_j > 0), with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Consequently Φ_j|Ω_j is injective, DΦ_j(w) is injective for w ∈ Ω_j (|DΦ_j(w)u| ≥ c_j|u|), Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact hence Borel, (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz hence Borel, Φ_j maps Lⁿ-null subsets of Ω_j to Hⁿ-null sets and Φ_j⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ_j(Ω_j) to Lⁿ-null sets. Put A_j(w) := DΦ_j(w) and T_j(w) := range A_j(w) (an n-dimensional subspace). As in the co-area formula, by the C¹ approximation theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5) there are C¹ functions h_{jk} on ℝⁿ and Borel A_{jk} ⊆ Ω_j with Lⁿ(Ω_j ∖ ⋃_k A_{jk}) = 0 on which f∘Φ_j is differentiable, f∘Φ_j = h_{jk} and D(f∘Φ_j) = Dh_{jk}. Directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10). Let Φ be C¹ near w, x = Φ(w), F : ℝ^P → ℝ Lipschitz with constant C, and suppose F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, s ↦ F(x + s DΦ(w)u) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)u at s = 0: indeed F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(x) = [F(Φ(w+su)) − F(Φ(w))] + [F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(Φ(w+su))], the first bracket is sD(F∘Φ)(w)u + o(s), and the second is bounded by C|Φ(w) + sDΦ(w)u − Φ(w+su)| = o(s). Tangent identification (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⟹' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version): if M' ⊆ U is Hᵏ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M' and θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M' ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, and Ψ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P is C¹ on an open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound on V, then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ Ψ(V) the pair (M', θ) has weighted approximate tangent plane range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x) at x. (For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), r^{-k}∫_{M'} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z) dHᵏ(z) splits into θ(x)·r^{-k}∫_{Ψ(V)} φ((z−x)/r) dHᵏ, which tends to θ(x)∫_{range DΨ} φ dHᵏ because Ψ(V) is a C¹ k-submanifold at x; the error r^{-k}∫_{M'∩Ψ(V)} φ(·)(θ − θ(x)) dHᵏ, which tends to 0 at Lebesgue points of θ for the Radon measure Hᵏ⌞(M'∩Ψ(V)∩K); and the parts over Ψ(V) ∖ M' and M' ∖ Ψ(V), which tend to 0 at Hᵏ-a.e. point of M' ∩ Ψ(V) by the upper-density theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, since Hᵏ⌞(Ψ(V)∖M') and θHᵏ⌞(M'∖Ψ(V)) are locally finite and vanish on M' ∩ Ψ(V).) Uniqueness at θ(x) > 0 then identifies every weighted approximate tangent plane at such x with range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x). Let Z₂ ⊆ M be the Hⁿ-null set consisting of M ∖ ⋃_{jk}Φ_j(A_{jk}) together with the points of M where the orientation clause of IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ fails, where TG(f, G) fails, or where (for some j with x ∈ Φ_j(Ω_j)) the tangent identification with Ψ = Φ_j fails. For x ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∖ Z₂ and w := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹x we then have: T_x = T_j(w) = span τ with τ orthonormal and ξ(x) = ±simple(τ); G(x) ∈ T_x; and for u ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨G(x), A_j(w)u⟩ = D(f∘Φ_j)(w)u = Dh_{jk}(w)u, i.e. A_j(w)ᵀG(x) = ∇h_{jk}(w).
8. (countablyRectifiable; Simon Ch. 3, 2.10(2).) For t ∈ ℝ let Σ_{jk}(t) := Φ_j({w ∈ Ω_j : h_{jk}(w) = t, ∇h_{jk}(w) ≠ 0}). By the implicit function theorem the set {w ∈ Ω_j : h_{jk}(w) = t, ∇h_{jk}(w) ≠ 0} is covered by countably many C¹ parametrizations ψ : V → ℝⁿ (V ⊆ ℝ^m open, Dψ injective, ψ bi-Lipschitz on V after shrinking), and Ψ := Φ_j∘ψ is C¹, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound; so Σ_{jk}(t) is a countable union of such chart images Ψ(V); extending Ψ|V componentwise by McShane (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) to a Lipschitz map ℝ^m → ℝ^P shows that each Ψ(V) lies in the range of a Lipschitz map, so Σ_{jk}(t) is countably m-rectifiable. (For m = 0, n = 1, the set {w ∈ Ω_j : h_{jk}(w) = t, h_{jk}'(w) ≠ 0} consists of isolated points, hence is countable, and every point is the range of a constant map on ℝ⁰.) If x ∈ M_t ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∖ Z₂ and w = (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹x, then h_{jk}(w) = f(x) = t and ∇h_{jk}(w) = A_j(w)ᵀG(x) ≠ 0 (G(x) ∈ range A_j(w) ∖ {0} and A_j(w)ᵀ is injective on range A_j(w)), so x ∈ Σ_{jk}(t). Thus M_t ⊆ ⋃_{jk}Σ_{jk}(t) ∪ (Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t}); for a.e. t the last set is H^m-null by NT, hence countably m-rectifiable (`countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero`), and M_t is countably m-rectifiable (`countablyRectifiable_iUnion`, `CountablyRectifiable.mono`).
9. (Tangent plane of the slice; Simon 4.1(2).) For x ∈ M with G(x) ≠ 0 at which T_x exists put T'_x := {v ∈ T_x : ⟨G(x), v⟩ = 0}, an m-dimensional subspace with T_x = T'_x ⊕ ℝG(x). Let x ∈ M_t ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∖ Z₂ and w := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹x; by Step 8, x ∈ Σ_{jk}(t), and by Step 7, ∇h_{jk}(w) = A_j(w)ᵀG(x), so the tangent plane of Σ_{jk}(t) at x is A_j(w)(ker Dh_{jk}(w)) = T'_x (for v = A_j(w)u, Dh_{jk}(w)u = ⟨A_j(w)ᵀG(x), u⟩ = ⟨G(x), v⟩). These sets M_t ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∖ Z₂ (over all j, k) cover M_t ∖ (Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t}) by Step 7. Fix t outside the null sets of Steps 4, 5, 8 and of NT for Z₂. Case m ≥ 1: by Steps 4 and 5, M_t is H^m-null-measurable and θ is positive and locally H^m-integrable on M_t in U, so the tangent identification with k = m, M' = M_t and each of the countably many charts Ψ = Φ_j∘ψ of Σ_{jk}(t) (Step 8) gives: for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t ∩ Ψ(V), a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at x exists and every such plane equals range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x), the tangent plane of Σ_{jk}(t) at x, which is T'_x when moreover x ∈ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∖ Z₂. Since the sets M_t ∩ Φ_j(A_{jk}) ∩ Ψ(V) ∖ Z₂ cover M_t ∖ (Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t}) and H^m(Z₂ ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0, for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at x exists and every one equals T'_x. Case m = 0: H⁰ = μHE[0] is counting measure (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero`, `hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`). Let x ∈ M_t and choose ρ > 0 with closedBall x ρ ⊆ U (U open); by Step 4 with K = closedBall x ρ, Σ_{z∈M_t∩K} θ(z) < ∞. Let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0) and 0 < r < ρ/R. Since blowUpMap x r is a bijection with inverse y ↦ x + ry, ∫ over the image (blowUpMap x r)(M_t) of φ(y)θ(x+ry) dH⁰(y) = Σ_{z∈M_t} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z), and only z with |z − x| < rR < ρ, i.e. z ∈ M_t ∩ K, contribute. Each term with z ≠ x vanishes once r < |z − x|/R, the term z = x equals φ(0)θ(x), and all terms are dominated by sup|φ|·θ(z)1_K(z), which is summable. By dominated convergence the expression tends to φ(0)θ(x) = θ(x)∫_{{0}} φ dH⁰ as r ↓ 0. As finrank {0} = 0, the subspace {0} = span(∅) is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at every x ∈ M_t, and T'_x = {0} (T_x is the line ℝG(x)).
10. (orients; Simon 4.3.) For a.e. t and H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t (x ∉ Z₂ and outside the exceptional set of Step 9): let τ'₁,…,τ'_m be an orthonormal basis of T'_x (empty for m = 0) and τ'_{m+1} := ν(x) = G(x)/|G(x)|. Then (τ'₁,…,τ'_{m+1}) is an orthonormal basis of T_x = span τ, so ξ(x) = ±simple(τ') by Fact F. For α ∈ Λ^m, using the formula for ν♭∧α with ⟨ν, τ'_i⟩ = 0 (i ≤ m) and ⟨ν, τ'_{m+1}⟩ = 1: ξ_t(x)(α) = ξ(x)(ν♭∧α) = ±(ν♭∧α)(τ'₁,…,τ'_{m+1}) = ±(−1)^m α(τ'₁,…,τ'_m). Hence ξ_t(x) = ±simple(τ'₁,…,τ'_m) with τ' := (τ'₁,…,τ'_m) orthonormal and span τ' = T'_x, which by Step 9 is the weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at x: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M_t θ x (span τ').
11. (Conclusion.) For t outside the countable union of the L¹-null sets above, Steps 3–10 give the seven fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, countablyRectifiable, pos, integrableOn, aestronglyMeasurable and orients of IsRectifiableTriple U m M_t θ ξ_t. ∎
proof_key_steps: Null transfer from the sibling co-area formula: Hⁿ-null subsets of M have H^m-null slices for a.e. t.
Co-area with 1_{K_i}θ̃: θ is locally H^m-integrable on M_t for a.e. t; Borel modifications give measurability of M_t and ξ_t.

C¹ charts plus C¹ approximation: away from a null set, M_t lies in the C¹ m-manifolds Φ_j{h_{jk} = t, ∇h_{jk} ≠ 0} (implicit function theorem), so M_t is countably m-rectifiable (Simon Ch. 3, 2.10(2)).
Tangent plane of (M_t, θ) is T_xM ∩ G(x)^⊥ a.e. (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6, 1.8(1) in dimension m; direct counting-measure computation for m = 0).
Orientation (Simon 4.3): with an adapted orthonormal frame, ξ⌞(G/|G|) = ±simple frame of T_xM ∩ G^⊥.

subproblems.title: Leibniz identity for Lipschitz multipliers on rectifiable currents (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.5(2), (1)–(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, and T ∈ D_n(U) with T(η) = ∫_M θ⟨η, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (= tauAction n M θ ξ η) for all η ∈ D^n(U). Let (μ, v) be a measure representation of T and (μ', v') one of ∂T (IsMeasureRepresentation). Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be L_h-Lipschitz and G_h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G_h| ≤ L_h everywhere and the tangential-gradient property for h (for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x: G_h(x) ∈ Q and d/ds h(x+su)|₀ = ⟨G_h(x), u⟩ for u ∈ Q). Then for every ω ∈ D^m(U): ∫ h⟨v', ω⟩ dμ' − ∫ h⟨v, dω⟩ dμ = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(G_h(x)♭∧ω(x)) dHⁿ(x), where G_h(x)♭∧ω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (G_h x)).smulRight (ω x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U (m + 1) M θ ξ → (∀ η : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T η = tauAction (m + 1) M θ ξ η) → ∀ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (μ' : Measure (Eucl P)) (v' : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) m), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → IsMeasureRepresentation T.boundary μ' v' → ∀ (h : Eucl P → ℝ) (Lh : ℝ≥0) (Gh : Eucl P → Eucl P), LipschitzWith Lh h → Measurable Gh → (∀ x, ‖Gh x‖ ≤ Lh) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m + 1) M θ x Q → Gh x ∈ Q ∧ ∀ u ∈ Q, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => h (x + s • u)) (inner ℝ (Gh x) u) 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, (∫ x, h x * v' x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ∂μ') - (∫ x, h x * v x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ∂μ) = ∫ x in M, θ x * ξ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (Gh x)).smulRight ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x))) ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P; Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure Lᵏ on ℝᵏ; H⁰ is counting measure by `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero` and `hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`). n := m+1. A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-form), ‖α‖ its operator norm; a k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k = (Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ); simple(τ) := simpleNVector τ, simple(τ)(α) = α(τ). For w ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^k put w♭∧α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α) ∈ Λ^{k+1}; by `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, (w♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i ⟨w, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_k); it is bilinear in (w, α), ‖w♭∧α‖ ≤ (k+1)|w|‖α‖, and it equals ((alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) k) (innerSL ℝ w))) α by `rfl`. Fact U: if τ is orthonormal and w = ±simple(τ) then |w(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖. Fact F (frame sign): if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the same k-dimensional subspace, τ'_i = Σ_j B_ij τ_j with B orthogonal, then by multilinearity and alternation simple(τ') = det(B)·simple(τ) and det B = ±1. IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ means: M ⊆ U; M is Hᵏ-null-measurable; M is countably k-rectifiable; θ > 0 on M; θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simple(τ). The weighted approximate tangent plane (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is unique at points where θ(x) ≠ 0 (SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`); when it exists at x ∈ M we call it T_x. TG(f, G) abbreviates the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and for every u ∈ Q the map s ↦ f(x + s u) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0.
We follow the printed proof of Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2), equations (1)–(3) (with the representations (2.7) of T and ∂T supplied as hypotheses). Fix ω ∈ D^m(U) and put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U.
1. (Preliminaries.) By IsMeasureRepresentation, x ↦ v'(x)(ω(x)) is μ'-integrable and x ↦ v(x)(dω(x)) is μ-integrable, where dω := exteriorDerivative ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport dω ⊆ K (`tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`). Both integrands vanish off K (v'(x), v(x) are linear and ω, dω vanish off K), and h is bounded on K, so h·v'(ω) ∈ L¹(μ') and h·v(dω) ∈ L¹(μ). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (orientation clause) there is an orthonormal basis τ(x) of the weighted tangent plane T_x with ξ(x) = ±simple(τ(x)); hence |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (Fact U).
2. (The field Y.) For x ∈ ℝ^P put Y(x) := θ(x)Σ_{i=1}^{P} ξ(x)(e_i♭∧ω(x)) e_i, so that ⟨Y(x), w⟩ = θ(x)ξ(x)(w♭∧ω(x)) for every w ∈ ℝ^P (linearity of w ↦ w♭∧ω(x)). Y is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off K, and |Y| ≤ (m+1)√P·θ·sup|ω| Hⁿ-a.e. on M; as θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)), Y ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M). If w ⊥ T_x then (w♭∧ω(x))(τ(x)) = Σ_i (−1)^{i−1}⟨w, τ_i(x)⟩ω(x)(…) = 0, so ⟨Y(x), w⟩ = 0; hence Y(x) ∈ T_x for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M. The right-hand side of the claim equals ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ (an absolutely convergent integral since |G_h| ≤ L_h).
3. (Mollification.) Let ρ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, support in the closed σ-ball, ∫ρ_σ = 1) and h_σ := ρ_σ * h. Then h_σ is C^∞ (`HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left`), L_h-Lipschitz, |∇h_σ| ≤ L_h and |h_σ − h| ≤ L_h σ everywhere (|h_σ(x) − h(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_σ(z)|h(x−z) − h(x)| dz).
4. (Leibniz rule for h_σ; Simon's (2).) The form h_σω is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ K, so h_σω ∈ D^m(U). By the product rule fderiv(h_σω)(x) = (Dh_σ(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) + h_σ(x)Dω(x) (`fderiv_smul`) and linearity of alternatizeUncurryFin, d(h_σω) = η_σ + h_σdω pointwise, where η_σ(x) := ∇h_σ(x)♭∧ω(x) (Dh_σ(x) = innerSL ℝ (∇h_σ(x))). Both η_σ and h_σdω are C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ K, i.e. lie in D^n(U). Hence, by linearity of T and the definition of the boundary (`GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply`), ∂T(h_σω) = T(η_σ) + T(h_σdω). By the representations, ∂T(h_σω) = ∫ v'(h_σω) dμ' = ∫ h_σ v'(ω) dμ' and T(h_σdω) = ∫ h_σ v(dω) dμ. Therefore (★) T(η_σ) = ∫ h_σ v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h_σ v(dω) dμ.
5. (σ ↓ 0 on the right of (★).) |∫(h_σ − h)v'(ω) dμ'| ≤ L_hσ‖v'(ω)‖_{L¹(μ')} → 0 and likewise for v(dω); hence T(η_σ) → ∫ h v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h v(dω) dμ, the left-hand side of the claim.
6. (Tau side; Simon's (3).) By hypothesis T(η_σ) = ∫_M θ ξ(η_σ) dHⁿ = ∫_M ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ (Step 2).
7. (Weak convergence; Simon's (1).) Claim: ∫_M ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ as σ ↓ 0. Charts (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3). Since M is countably n-rectifiable, M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and N_j embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifolds of ℝ^P. Covering every N_j by countably many relatively compact coordinate patches we obtain countably many open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ and C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P which are Lipschitz on Ω_j and satisfy c_j|w − w'| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w')| (w, w' ∈ Ω_j, some c_j > 0), with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Consequently Φ_j|Ω_j is injective, DΦ_j(w) is injective for w ∈ Ω_j (|DΦ_j(w)u| ≥ c_j|u|), Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact hence Borel, (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz hence Borel, Φ_j maps Lⁿ-null subsets of Ω_j to Hⁿ-null sets and Φ_j⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ_j(Ω_j) to Lⁿ-null sets. Put A_j(w) := DΦ_j(w) and T_j(w) := range A_j(w) (an n-dimensional subspace). Let V_j := Φ_j(Ω_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j}Φ_i(Ω_i) (disjoint Borel). Since |⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩| ≤ L_h|Y| ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M) uniformly in σ and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃V_j) = 0, dominated convergence for the series over j (`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence` or dominated convergence for ∫_M = Σ_j ∫_{M∩V_j}) reduces the claim to: for each j, ∫_{M∩V_j} ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_{M∩V_j} ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ.
8. (One chart.) Fix j and write Φ, Ω, A(w) := DΦ(w), JΦ(w) := √det(A(w)ᵀA(w)) (continuous, between c_jⁿ and Lip(Φ|Ω)ⁿ on Ω). Tangent identification (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⟹' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version): if M' ⊆ U is Hᵏ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M' and θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M' ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, and Ψ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P is C¹ on an open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound on V, then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ Ψ(V) the pair (M', θ) has weighted approximate tangent plane range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x) at x. (For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), r^{-k}∫_{M'} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z) dHᵏ(z) splits into θ(x)·r^{-k}∫_{Ψ(V)} φ((z−x)/r) dHᵏ, which tends to θ(x)∫_{range DΨ} φ dHᵏ because Ψ(V) is a C¹ k-submanifold at x; the error r^{-k}∫_{M'∩Ψ(V)} φ(·)(θ − θ(x)) dHᵏ, which tends to 0 at Lebesgue points of θ for the Radon measure Hᵏ⌞(M'∩Ψ(V)∩K); and the parts over Ψ(V) ∖ M' and M' ∖ Ψ(V), which tend to 0 at Hᵏ-a.e. point of M' ∩ Ψ(V) by the upper-density theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, since Hᵏ⌞(Ψ(V)∖M') and θHᵏ⌞(M'∖Ψ(V)) are locally finite and vanish on M' ∩ Ψ(V).) Uniqueness at θ(x) > 0 then identifies every weighted approximate tangent plane at such x with range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x). Directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10). Let Φ be C¹ near w, x = Φ(w), F : ℝ^P → ℝ Lipschitz with constant C, and suppose F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, s ↦ F(x + s DΦ(w)u) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)u at s = 0: indeed F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(x) = [F(Φ(w+su)) − F(Φ(w))] + [F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(Φ(w+su))], the first bracket is sD(F∘Φ)(w)u + o(s), and the second is bounded by C|Φ(w) + sDΦ(w)u − Φ(w+su)| = o(s). Let E := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹(M ∩ V_j). For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ E, with x = Φ(w): T_x = range A(w) (tangent identification with M' = M, Ψ = Φ; Φ⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets), Y(x) ∈ T_x, the tangential-gradient property of G_h holds at x, and h∘Φ is differentiable at w (Rademacher). Put a(w) := (A(w)ᵀA(w))⁻¹A(w)ᵀY(x), so Y(x) = A(w)a(w) and |a(w)| ≤ |Y(x)|/c_j. Then ⟨Y(x), ∇h_σ(x)⟩ = ⟨a(w), A(w)ᵀ∇h_σ(Φ(w))⟩ = ⟨a(w), ∇(h_σ∘Φ)(w)⟩ (chain rule), and ⟨Y(x), G_h(x)⟩ = Σ_i a_i(w)⟨G_h(x), ∂_iΦ(w)⟩ = Σ_i a_i(w) ∂_i(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨a(w), ∇(h∘Φ)(w)⟩, because ∂_iΦ(w) ∈ T_x, so ⟨G_h(x), ∂_iΦ(w)⟩ = d/ds h(x + s∂_iΦ(w))|₀, which equals ∂_i(h∘Φ)(w) by the directional-derivative fact. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ|Ω (Simon Ch. 2, 4.13; Federer 3.2.3/3.2.5), ∫_{M∩V_j} F dHⁿ = ∫_E F(Φ(w))JΦ(w) dw for F ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M∩V_j)). With c(w) := 1_E(w)JΦ(w)a(w), which lies in L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ) since ∫|c| ≤ c_j⁻¹∫_{M∩V_j}|Y| dHⁿ, we get ∫_{M∩V_j}⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_Ω ⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ dw and ∫_{M∩V_j}⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_Ω ⟨c, ∇u⟩ dw, where u_σ := h_σ∘Φ and u := h∘Φ.
9. (Weak-* convergence of gradients.) u_σ → u uniformly on Ω (|h_σ − h| ≤ L_hσ), and |∇u_σ|, |∇u| ≤ L_h·Lip(Φ|Ω) (a.e. for u). For c' ∈ C_c^1(Ω; ℝⁿ), ∫⟨c', ∇u_σ⟩ = −∫u_σ div c' → −∫u div c' = ∫⟨c', ∇u⟩: the last equality is integration by parts for the locally Lipschitz u, obtained from Fubini's theorem and the absolute continuity of u on almost every line parallel to a coordinate axis, where the partial derivatives exist a.e. and coincide with those of the Rademacher differential. For general c ∈ L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ) and δ > 0 choose c' ∈ C_c^1 with ‖c − c'‖_{L¹} < δ (density); then limsup_σ |∫⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ − ∫⟨c, ∇u⟩| ≤ 2L_hLip(Φ|Ω)δ. Hence ∫_Ω⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ → ∫_Ω⟨c, ∇u⟩, which with Step 8 proves the claim of Step 7.
10. (Conclusion.) By Steps 5, 6 and 7, ∫ h v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h v(dω) dμ = lim_{σ↓0} T(η_σ) = ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ ξ(G_h♭∧ω) dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Integrability of h·v'(ω), h·v(dω); unit simple ξ; the L¹ field Y with ⟨Y, w⟩ = θξ(w♭∧ω), tangent to M a.e.
Mollify h; Leibniz rule d(h_σω) = ∇h_σ♭∧ω + h_σdω and the representations give T(∇h_σ♭∧ω) = ∫h_σv'(ω)dμ' − ∫h_σv(dω)dμ.
σ ↓ 0 on the representation side by uniform convergence h_σ → h.
Tau side: T(∇h_σ♭∧ω) = ∫_M⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩dHⁿ.
Weak convergence ∫_M⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ → ∫_M⟨Y, G_h⟩ via C¹ charts, Simon Ch. 2 4.10, the area formula and weak-* convergence of D(h_σ∘Φ) (Simon 4.5(2), (1)).

subproblems.title: Each slice agrees with the integer multiplicity slice on a fixed form for a.e. t (Simon Ch. 6, 4.2 and 4.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, T ∈ D_n(U) with T(η) = tauAction n M θ ξ η for all η ∈ D^n(U), f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G| ≤ L everywhere and the tangential-gradient property for f (for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x: G(x) ∈ Q and d/ds f(x+su)|₀ = ⟨G(x), u⟩ for u ∈ Q). Let M_t := {x ∈ M : f(x) = t, G(x) ≠ 0} and ξ_t(x) := ξ(x)⌞(|G(x)|⁻¹G(x)) as in the slice triple (ξ_t(x)(α) = ξ(x)((|G(x)|⁻¹G(x))♭∧α)). Then for every ω ∈ D^m(U) there is an L¹-null set F_ω such that for every t ∉ F_ω and every S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S, S(ω) = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω = ∫_{M_t} θ(x)ξ_t(x)(ω(x)) dH^m(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U (m + 1) M θ ξ → (∀ η : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T η = tauAction (m + 1) M θ ξ η) → LipschitzWith L f → Measurable G → (∀ x, ‖G x‖ ≤ L) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m + 1) M θ x Q → G x ∈ Q ∧ ∀ u ∈ Q, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => f (x + s • u)) (inner ℝ (G x) u) 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn U m, IsSlice T f t S → S ω = tauAction m {x | x ∈ M ∧ f x = t ∧ G x ≠ 0} θ (fun x => (ξ x).comp ((ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) m) (innerSL ℝ (‖G x‖⁻¹ • G x))))) ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P; Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure Lᵏ on ℝᵏ; H⁰ is counting measure by `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero` and `hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`). n := m+1. A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-form), ‖α‖ its operator norm; a k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k = (Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ); simple(τ) := simpleNVector τ, simple(τ)(α) = α(τ). For w ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^k put w♭∧α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α) ∈ Λ^{k+1}; by `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, (w♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i ⟨w, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_k); it is bilinear in (w, α), ‖w♭∧α‖ ≤ (k+1)|w|‖α‖, and it equals ((alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) k) (innerSL ℝ w))) α by `rfl`. Fact U: if τ is orthonormal and w = ±simple(τ) then |w(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖. Fact F (frame sign): if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the same k-dimensional subspace, τ'_i = Σ_j B_ij τ_j with B orthogonal, then by multilinearity and alternation simple(τ') = det(B)·simple(τ) and det B = ±1. IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ means: M ⊆ U; M is Hᵏ-null-measurable; M is countably k-rectifiable; θ > 0 on M; θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simple(τ). The weighted approximate tangent plane (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is unique at points where θ(x) ≠ 0 (SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`); when it exists at x ∈ M we call it T_x. TG(f, G) abbreviates the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and for every u ∈ Q the map s ↦ f(x + s u) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0.
We follow the printed proof of Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2), from (4) to the end, with Remark 4.2, evaluating the restriction terms in the representations supplied by IsSlice. The siblings `coarea` and `lipschitz_leibniz` apply to the present hypotheses verbatim. Fix ω ∈ D^m(U), K := tsupport ω (compact ⊆ U), and write ν(x) := |G(x)|⁻¹G(x) (so ν(x) = 0 when G(x) = 0).
1. (G vanishes on level sets; Simon's remark after (4).) For c ∈ ℝ apply `coarea` to the Borel g := 1_{f⁻¹{c}}: ∫_ℝ H^m(M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ f⁻¹{c}) dt = ∫_M |G|1_{f=c} dHⁿ. The left integrand vanishes for t ≠ c, so the left side is 0 and G = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ f⁻¹{c}.
2. (Null transfer, NT.) As in the slice triple: for Z ⊆ M with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, applying `coarea` to g = 1_{toMeasurable Hⁿ Z} gives H^m(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 for a.e. t.
3. (The density g_ω.) Let θ̃, ξ̃ be Borel with θ = θ̃, ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ-a.e. on M (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M since M ⊆ U is covered by countably many compacts K_i ⊆ U on which θ is integrable). Define the Borel function g(x) := 1_K(x)1_{G(x)≠0}θ̃(x)ξ̃(x)(ν(x)♭∧ω(x)). By Fact U and ‖ν♭∧ω(x)‖ ≤ (m+1)‖ω(x)‖, |g| ≤ (m+1)sup‖ω‖·θ̃·1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so g ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M). Moreover θξ(G♭∧ω) = |G|·g Hⁿ-a.e. on M (both vanish where G = 0; elsewhere G♭∧ω = |G|ν♭∧ω by linearity, and ω = 0 off K).
4. (Remark 4.2.) Write g = g⁺ − g⁻ and φ_±(r) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{r}} g^± dH^m. By `coarea`, φ_± are a.e.-measurable with ∫_ℝ φ_± dr = ∫_M |G|g^± dHⁿ ≤ L‖g‖_{L¹(Hⁿ⌞M)} < ∞; so φ_± < ∞ a.e. and φ := φ₊ − φ₋ ∈ L¹(ℝ). For a < b apply `coarea` to the Borel g^±·1_{a<f<b}: on f⁻¹{r} this function equals 1_{(a,b)}(r)g^±, hence ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} |G|g^± dHⁿ = ∫_a^b φ_±(r) dr and, subtracting the finite quantities, ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} |G|g dHⁿ = ∫_a^b φ(r) dr.
5. (Identification with the slice.) Let Z := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≠ θ̃(x) or ξ(x) ≠ ξ̃(x)} (Hⁿ-null). For t with H^m(Z ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 (a.e. t by NT) and φ_±(t) < ∞: g is H^m-integrable on M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, it agrees H^m-a.e. there with 1_{G≠0}θξ(ν♭∧ω), and since {G ≠ 0} is Borel and M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ {G ≠ 0} = M_t (`setIntegral_indicator`), φ(t) = ∫_{M_t} θ(x)ξ(x)(ν(x)♭∧ω(x)) dH^m = ∫_{M_t} θ(x)ξ_t(x)(ω(x)) dH^m = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω (the factor 1_K is irrelevant because ω = 0 off K, and ξ_t(x)(α) = ξ(x)(ν(x)♭∧α) by definition and `rfl`).
6. (Lebesgue points.) By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem (`IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average` for Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with centres t − ε/2, radii ε/2 and K = 1), for a.e. t: ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^{t} φ(r) dr → φ(t) as ε ↓ 0. Let F_ω be the union of the L¹-null sets of Steps 5 and 6; it depends only on (M, θ, ξ, f, G, ω).
7. (Cut-offs; Simon's ψ.) Fix t ∉ F_ω and S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S: there are A ∈ D_n(U), B ∈ D_m(U), a representation (μ, v) of T and a representation (μ', v') of ∂T with A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ, B(ϖ) = ∫_{A_t} v'(ϖ) dμ' for all test forms, A_t := {x ∈ U : f(x) < t} (Borel), and S(ϖ) = A(dϖ) − B(ϖ). For 0 < ε let ψ_ε(s) := 1 for s ≤ t − ε, (t − s)/ε for t − ε ≤ s ≤ t, 0 for s ≥ t; h_ε := ψ_ε∘f is (L/ε)-Lipschitz with 0 ≤ h_ε ≤ 1; and G_ε(x) := −ε⁻¹1_{(t−ε,t)}(f(x))G(x), Borel with |G_ε| ≤ L/ε. Tangential-gradient property for (h_ε, G_ε): let x ∈ M satisfy TG(f, G) and lie outside the Hⁿ-null sets of Step 1 for c = t − ε and c = t, and let Q be a weighted tangent plane at x and u ∈ Q. Then G_ε(x) ∈ Q. If f(x) ∉ [t−ε, t], ψ_ε is constant near f(x) and f is continuous, so s ↦ h_ε(x+su) is constant near 0: derivative 0 = ⟨G_ε(x), u⟩. If t−ε < f(x) < t, ψ_ε is affine with slope −1/ε near f(x), so the derivative is −ε⁻¹⟨G(x), u⟩ = ⟨G_ε(x), u⟩ (chain rule). If f(x) ∈ {t−ε, t}, then G(x) = 0, so f(x+su) − f(x) = o(s) and |h_ε(x+su) − h_ε(x)| ≤ ε⁻¹|f(x+su) − f(x)| = o(s): derivative 0 = ⟨G_ε(x), u⟩.
8. (Apply the Leibniz identity; Simon's (2)–(4).) `lipschitz_leibniz` with (μ, v), (μ', v'), h = h_ε, L_h = L/ε, G_h = G_ε gives ∫ h_εv'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h_εv(dω) dμ = ∫_M θξ(G_ε♭∧ω) dHⁿ = −ε⁻¹∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θξ(G♭∧ω) dHⁿ = −ε⁻¹∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} |G|g dHⁿ = −ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^{t} φ(r) dr (Steps 3 and 4; G_ε♭∧ω = −ε⁻¹1_{(t−ε,t)}(f)G♭∧ω by linearity).
9. (ε ↓ 0.) As ε ↓ 0, h_ε → 1_{f<t} pointwise on ℝ^P (if f(x) < t then h_ε(x) = 1 once ε ≤ t − f(x); if f(x) ≥ t then h_ε(x) = 0), with |h_ε| ≤ 1; v'(ω) ∈ L¹(μ'), v(dω) ∈ L¹(μ), and both vanish off K ⊆ U, so 1_{f<t}v'(ω) = 1_{A_t}v'(ω) and 1_{f<t}v(dω) = 1_{A_t}v(dω). By dominated convergence, ∫ h_εv'(ω) dμ' → ∫_{A_t} v'(ω) dμ' = B(ω) and ∫ h_εv(dω) dμ → ∫_{A_t} v(dω) dμ = A(dω), where A(dω) = A.boundary(ω) (`GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply`). The right side of Step 8 tends to −φ(t) by Step 6. Hence B(ω) − A(dω) = −φ(t), so S(ω) = A(dω) − B(ω) = φ(t) = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω by Step 5. Since F_ω does not depend on S, this proves: for a.e. t, every S with IsSlice T f t S satisfies S(ω) = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: Co-area: G = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on every level set of f, and Hⁿ-null subsets of M have H^m-null slices for a.e. t.
Borel L¹ density g = 1_K1_{G≠0}θ̃ξ̃(ν♭∧ω) with θξ(G♭∧ω) = |G|g; Remark 4.2: ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}}|G|g = ∫_a^b φ, φ ∈ L¹(ℝ).
For a.e. t, φ(t) = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω; Lebesgue differentiation at a.e. t; F_ω is independent of S.
Piecewise-linear cut-off h_ε = ψ_ε∘f with tangential gradient −ε⁻¹1_{t−ε<f<t}G; the Leibniz sibling with the IsSlice representations.
ε ↓ 0: dominated convergence gives B(ω) − A(dω) = −φ(t), i.e. S(ω) = tauAction m M_t θ ξ_t ω.

subproblems.title: A countable family of test forms determines currents
subproblems.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ and every open U ⊆ ℝ^P there is a countable set E ⊆ D^k(U) (= TestFormOn U k) such that any two currents S, R ∈ D_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) with S(e) = R(e) for all e ∈ E are equal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ E : Set (TestFormOn U k), E.Countable ∧ ∀ S R : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (∀ e ∈ E, S e = R e) → S = R
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k: C^∞ forms ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) k with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. D_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k: linear functionals S with S(ω_l) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω 0, i.e. there is a compact K ⊆ U containing all tsupport ω_l and, for every i ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω_l → 0 uniformly on K. This realizes Simon's 'countable dense set of ω ∈ Dⁿ(U)' in the proof of 4.5(2).
1. (Exhaustion.) Choose compacts K_j ⊆ U (j ≥ 1) such that every compact subset of U lies in some K_j (e.g. K_j := {x : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}, or closedBall 0 j if U = ℝ^P; any compact C ⊆ U has positive distance to ℝ^P ∖ U and is bounded).
2. (Separability.) Fix j and let D_j := {ω ∈ D^k(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K_j}. For i ∈ ℕ let F_i be the finite-dimensional normed space of continuous i-multilinear maps (ℝ^P)^i → Covector (Eucl P) k and consider ι_j : D_j → X_j := Π_{i∈ℕ} C(K_j, F_i), ι_j(ω) := (x ↦ iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω x)_{i} restricted to K_j (continuous since ω is C^∞). Each C(K_j, F_i) (compact-open = uniform topology, as K_j is compact) is second countable (`ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology` from Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace: K_j is second countable and locally compact, F_i second countable), so the countable product X_j is second countable, hence so is the subspace ι_j(D_j); in particular it is separable and first countable. Choose a countable E_j ⊆ D_j with ι_j(E_j) dense in ι_j(D_j).
3. (Approximating sequences.) Let E := ⋃_j E_j (countable). Given ω ∈ D^k(U), tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so tsupport ω ⊆ K_j for some j and ω ∈ D_j. By density and first countability there are e_l ∈ E_j with ι_j(e_l) → ι_j(ω), i.e. for every i, iteratedFDeriv ℝ i e_l → iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω uniformly on K_j. Put ϖ_l := e_l − ω ∈ D^k(U). Then tsupport ϖ_l ⊆ tsupport e_l ∪ tsupport ω ⊆ K_j, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ K_j, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ϖ_l = iteratedFDeriv ℝ i e_l − iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω (`iteratedFDeriv_sub`, both C^∞) → 0 uniformly on K_j, while iteratedFDeriv ℝ i 0 = 0. Hence TestFormOnConverges ϖ 0 with K := K_j.
4. (Conclusion.) Let S, R ∈ D_k(U) agree on E. By the continuity field of GeometricCurrentOn, S(ϖ_l) → 0 and R(ϖ_l) → 0. By linearity, S(ω) − R(ω) = (S(e_l) − S(ϖ_l)) − (R(e_l) − R(ϖ_l)) = R(ϖ_l) − S(ϖ_l) → 0, so S(ω) = R(ω). As ω was arbitrary, S = R (`GeometricCurrentOn.ext`). ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_j of the open set U.
Forms supported in K_j embed, via all iterated derivatives restricted to K_j, into a second countable countable product of C(K_j, F_i); pick a countable dense E_j.
Every test form is the D(U)-limit of a sequence from E = ⋃E_j (TestFormOnConverges of the differences).
Sequential continuity and linearity of currents: agreement on E forces equality.

subproblems.title: A rectifiable triple defines a current τ(M, θ, ξ) (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1)
subproblems.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) with IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ, there is a current R ∈ D_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) with R(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every ω ∈ D^k(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k), IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → ∃ R : GeometricCurrentOn U k, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, R ω = tauAction k M θ ξ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. Hᵏ := μHE[k]; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of a k-covector. By the orientation field of IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ, for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every k-covector α (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm`).
1. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ D^k(U) and K := tsupport ω, compact and ⊆ U. The integrand F_ω(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes for x ∉ K. On M ∩ K it is Hᵏ-a.e. strongly measurable (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ K as it is integrable there, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable on M, ω is continuous, and evaluation (w, α) ↦ w(α) is continuous) and |F_ω| ≤ sup_x‖ω(x)‖·|θ| Hᵏ-a.e. on M ∩ K. Since θ ∈ L¹(Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ K)) (integrableOn field) and ω is bounded (continuous with compact support), F_ω ∈ L¹(Hᵏ⌞M) (write F_ω = 1_K·F_ω; `IntegrableOn` of M ∩ K extended by zero).
2. (Linearity.) For ω, ω' ∈ D^k(U) and a, b ∈ ℝ, F_{aω+bω'} = aF_ω + bF_{ω'} pointwise (ξ(x) is linear), so by Step 1 and linearity of the integral, tauAction k M θ ξ (aω + bω') = a·tauAction k M θ ξ ω + b·tauAction k M θ ξ ω'. Thus R₀(ω) := tauAction k M θ ξ ω defines a linear map TestFormOn U k →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
3. (Continuity.) Let ω_l ∈ D^k(U) with TestFormOnConverges ω 0: a compact K ⊆ U contains every tsupport ω_l and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_l → 0 uniformly on K; since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_l x‖ = ‖ω_l(x)‖ (`norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero`), ε_l := sup_{x∈K}‖ω_l(x)‖ → 0, and ω_l = 0 off K. Then |R₀(ω_l)| ≤ ∫_{M∩K} |θ|·‖ω_l‖ dHᵏ ≤ ε_l·∫_{M∩K}|θ| dHᵏ → 0 (θ ∈ L¹(Hᵏ⌞(M∩K))).
4. (Conclusion.) R := ⟨R₀, Step 3⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U k, and R(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ D^k(U) by construction. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit simple orientation: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ a.e. on M.
θξ(ω) is integrable: supported in tsupport ω, dominated by sup‖ω‖·θ on M ∩ tsupport ω.
Linearity of the integral gives a linear functional on D^k(U).
Sequential continuity: |τ(ω_l)| ≤ sup_K‖ω_l‖·∫_{M∩K}θ → 0.
